A balanced beam scale showing 24 g of Mg and 16 g of O2 on the left pan, and 40 g of MgO on the right pan. Both sides are perfectly balanced.

A diagram showing two carbon oxides to illustrate the Law of Multiple Proportions. Top row: CO molecule (one black C atom, one red O atom). Bottom row: CO2 molecule (one black C atom, two red O atoms). Labels showing the mass ratio: "In CO, 12g C combines with 16g O", "In CO2, 12g C combines with 32g O", "Ratio of oxygen masses = 16:32 = 1:2".

Triangle diagram illustrating the Law of Reciprocal Proportions for S, H, and O. At the vertices: S, H, O. Sides connect S to H (H2S), S to O (SO2), and H to O (H2O). Labels around the edges show the mass combinations: "32g S + 2g H", "32g S + 32g O", and "2g H + 16g O (which scales to 32g O)".

Visual breakdown of the mole concept: A central circle, with three arrows pointing outwards. Arrow 1 points to "Mass in grams (Molar Mass)". Arrow 2 points to "6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's Number)". Arrow 3 points to "22.4 dm³ of gas at s.t.p. (Molar Volume)".
